`friendlycells` computes similarity between spatial transcriptomics samples based on which labels (e.g. cell types) border one another. Available for R and Python. Compatible with Visium, Visium HD (binned or segmented) and Xenium. ## Installation ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ```r remotes::install_github("george-hall-ucl/friendlycells", subdir = "R") ``` Requires `dbscan` and `deldir`. ## Python ```bash pip install "git+https://github.com/george-hall-ucl/friendlycells#subdirectory=python" ``` Requires `pandas`, `numpy` and `scipy`. ::: ## Usage Give `spatial_similarity()` one data frame per sample, with columns `x`, `y` (positions, e.g. in pixels or micrometres) and `label` (see [Extracting positions](reference.qmd#extracting-positions)): ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ```r library(friendlycells) samples <- list(sample_1 = df1, sample_2 = df2, sample_3 = df3) sim <- spatial_similarity(samples) ``` ## Python ```python from friendlycells import spatial_similarity samples = {"sample_1": df1, "sample_2": df2, "sample_3": df3} sim = spatial_similarity(samples) ``` ::: This returns a sample × sample matrix of similarity scores: 1 = identical, 0 = least similar pair. See the [example](#example) below, and the [Reference](reference.qmd) for all options, including how neighbors are computed. Different definitions of neighborhoods will lead to different results, and, unless told otherwise, `friendlycells` uses (hopefully) sensible defaults. For more information on different definitions of neighbourhood, see [here](neighborhoods.qmd). ## Example This example uses four mouse brain sections from 10x Genomics (two anterior, two posterior), with each spot labelled by its most enriched of five marker genes. ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="Setup: download and label the data, define plotting helpers"} # Requires Seurat, hdf5r and ggplot2. library(Seurat) library(ggplot2) markers <- c("Mbp", "Slc17a7", "Penk", "Hpca", "Gabra6") ids <- c(anterior_1 = "V1_Mouse_Brain_Sagittal_Anterior", anterior_2 = "V1_Mouse_Brain_Sagittal_Anterior_Section_2", posterior_1 = "V1_Mouse_Brain_Sagittal_Posterior", posterior_2 = "V1_Mouse_Brain_Sagittal_Posterior_Section_2") cache <- tools::R_user_dir("friendlycells", "cache") seurat_objects <- lapply(ids, function(id) { dir <- file.path(cache, id) if (!dir.exists(file.path(dir, "spatial"))) { url <- paste0("https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/spatial-exp/1.1.0/", id, "/", id) dir.create(dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE) download.file(paste0(url, "_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5"), file.path(dir, "filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5")) download.file(paste0(url, "_spatial.tar.gz"), tar <- tempfile()) untar(tar, exdir = dir) } cells <- Load10X_Spatial(dir) counts <- as.matrix(GetAssayData(cells, layer = "counts")[markers, ]) cells$cell_type <- markers[max.col(t(counts / rowMeans(counts)), ties.method = "first")] cells }) plot_slices <- function(samples) { spots <- do.call(rbind, Map(cbind, sample = names(samples), samples)) ggplot(spots, aes(.data$x, -.data$y, color = .data$label)) + geom_point(size = 1.1, stroke = 0) + facet_wrap(~sample, nrow = 1) + coord_fixed() + scale_color_manual(values = c("#CC79A7", "#D55E00", "#0072B2", "#F0E442", "#009E73")) + guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 4))) + theme_void(base_size = 14) + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_blank()) } plot_similarity <- function(sim) { df <- as.data.frame(as.table(sim)) lower <- df[as.integer(df$Var1) >= as.integer(df$Var2), ] ggplot(lower, aes(.data$Var1, .data$Var2, fill = .data$Freq)) + geom_tile() + geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", .data$Freq), color = .data$Freq < 0.1), size = 5, fontface = "bold", show.legend = FALSE) + scale_color_manual(values = c("black", "white")) + scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "inferno", name = "Similarity") + coord_fixed() + theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + theme(axis.title = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), text = element_text(face = "bold")) } ``` ::: Each sample is a data frame of spot positions (in full-resolution image pixels) and labels: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(friendlycells) samples <- lapply(seurat_objects, function(cells) { coords <- GetTissueCoordinates(cells) data.frame(x = coords$x, y = coords$y, label = cells$cell_type[coords$cell], row.names = coords$cell) }) head(samples$anterior_1) #> x y label #> AAACAAGTATCTCCCA-1 8500 7474 Mbp #> AAACACCAATAACTGC-1 2788 8552 Slc17a7 #> AAACAGAGCGACTCCT-1 7950 3163 Slc17a7 #> AAACAGCTTTCAGAAG-1 2100 6636 Mbp #> AAACAGGGTCTATATT-1 2375 7115 Penk #> AAACATGGTGAGAGGA-1 1480 8912 Slc17a7 ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_slices(samples) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/r-slices-1.png) ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} sim <- spatial_similarity(samples) #> Using neighborhood = "radius", as the positions lie on a grid. round(sim, 2) #> anterior_1 anterior_2 posterior_1 posterior_2 #> anterior_1 1.00 0.93 0.00 0.01 #> anterior_2 0.93 1.00 0.03 0.04 #> posterior_1 0.00 0.03 1.00 0.92 #> posterior_2 0.01 0.04 0.92 1.00 plot_similarity(sim) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/r-similarity-1.png){width=60%} ::: ::: ## Python ::: {.cell jupyter_compat='true'} ```{.python .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="Setup: download and label the data, define plotting helpers"} # Requires squidpy, matplotlib and seaborn. from pathlib import Path import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import numpy as np import pandas as pd import seaborn as sns import squidpy as sq markers = ["Mbp", "Slc17a7", "Penk", "Hpca", "Gabra6"] ids = { "anterior_1": "V1_Mouse_Brain_Sagittal_Anterior", "anterior_2": "V1_Mouse_Brain_Sagittal_Anterior_Section_2", "posterior_1": "V1_Mouse_Brain_Sagittal_Posterior", "posterior_2": "V1_Mouse_Brain_Sagittal_Posterior_Section_2", } cache = Path.home() / ".cache" / "friendlycells" adatas = {} labels = {} for name, sample_id in ids.items(): adata = sq.datasets.visium(sample_id, base_dir=cache) adata.var_names_make_unique() counts = adata[:, markers].X.toarray() top = (counts / counts.mean(axis=0)).argmax(axis=1) adatas[name] = adata labels[name] = np.array(markers)[top] def plot_slices(samples): palette = ["#CC79A7", "#D55E00", "#0072B2", "#F0E442", "#009E73"] colors = dict(zip(sorted(markers), palette)) fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(samples), layout="constrained") for ax, (name, df) in zip(axes, samples.items()): ax.scatter( df["x"], -df["y"], c=df["label"].map(colors), s=3, linewidths=0, ) ax.set_title(name) ax.set_aspect("equal") ax.axis("off") handles = [ plt.Line2D([], [], marker="o", linestyle="", color=color, label=label) for label, color in colors.items() ] fig.legend( handles=handles, loc="outside lower center", ncol=len(colors), frameon=False, ) plt.show() def plot_similarity(sim): style = {"font.size": 14, "font.weight": "bold", "figure.autolayout": True} with plt.rc_context(style): ax = sns.heatmap( sim, mask=np.tril(np.ones(sim.shape, dtype=bool), k=-1), annot=True, fmt=".2f", cmap="inferno", vmin=0, vmax=1, square=True, cbar_kws={"label": "Similarity"}, ) ax.invert_yaxis() plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha="right") plt.show() ``` ::: Each sample is a DataFrame of spot positions (in full-resolution image pixels) and labels: ::: {.cell jupyter_compat='true'} ```{.python .cell-code} from friendlycells import spatial_similarity samples = { name: pd.DataFrame({ "x": adata.obsm["spatial"][:, 0], "y": adata.obsm["spatial"][:, 1], "label": labels[name], }, index=adata.obs_names) for name, adata in adatas.items() } print(samples["anterior_1"].head()) #> x y label #> AAACAAGTATCTCCCA-1 8500 7474 Mbp #> AAACACCAATAACTGC-1 2788 8552 Slc17a7 #> AAACAGAGCGACTCCT-1 7950 3163 Slc17a7 #> AAACAGCTTTCAGAAG-1 2100 6636 Mbp #> AAACAGGGTCTATATT-1 2375 7115 Penk ``` ::: ::: {.cell jupyter_compat='true'} ```{.python .cell-code} plot_slices(samples) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/py-slices-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ::: {.cell jupyter_compat='true'} ```{.python .cell-code} sim = spatial_similarity(samples) #> Using neighborhood="radius", as the positions lie on a grid. print(sim.round(2)) #> anterior_1 anterior_2 posterior_1 posterior_2 #> anterior_1 1.00 0.93 0.00 0.01 #> anterior_2 0.93 1.00 0.03 0.04 #> posterior_1 0.00 0.03 1.00 0.92 #> posterior_2 0.01 0.04 0.92 1.00 plot_similarity(sim) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/py-similarity-3.png){width=60%} ::: ::: ::: The anterior sections are most similar to each other, as are the posterior sections, while anterior and posterior sections are dissimilar. ## Citation The original algorithm and implementation of `friendlycells` were first published in: - Durkin _et al_. "Functional integration of an autologous engineered esophagus in a large-animal model." _Nature Biotechnology_ (2026). - Budinger _et al_. "An in vivo and in vitro spatiotemporal profile of human midbrain development." _Nature Communications_ (2026).
